text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Telecommunications utility cuts rates for international calls and some local calls by up to 25 percent.
- State-owned railway grants pensioners a reduction of 40 percent on train fares except for shuttle service.
- United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan invites all parties in Western Sahara conflict to a second round of talks in London from July 19 to 20 following Lisbon meeting.
- Population ministry survey shows life expectancy is 68 years in Morocco.
- Police break up gang specialising in carrying illegal immigrants in makeshift boats from the northern city of Nador to Spain in return for up to 30,000 dirhams ($3,157).
